# Fixtures

These pages are **written, not captured**. They are generated by
`generate.go`, which is committed beside them and is the readable statement of
what each one models.

Why written: this repository publishes one product. Someone else's pages are
not ours to ship, and a few megabytes of captured HTML would be both a weight
and a liability. Every structure reproduced here was measured on live sessions
first — these are a rendering of those measurements, not a guess.

The attribute names are the real ones, because they are what the parser
anchors on: `data-ved` marks a telemetry-bearing link, `data-text-ad` marks a
text ad, `data-pcu` carries an advertiser's address, `role="heading"` titles a
result in the card layout. Their values are placeholders.

| File | What it models |
|---|---|
| `serp_goto_ru.html` | encrypted `/goto` links, titles in `h3`, `cite` present |
| `serp_cards_ru.html` | card layout — no `h3` and no `cite` at all, titles in `[role=heading]` |
| `serp_site_ru.html` | a `site:` query, the shape the index check reads |
| `serp_ads_us.html` | all three ad placements at once: top, bottom, product |
| `serp_direct_us.html` | plain `href` links instead of the redirector |
| `jsshell.html` | the JavaScript shell: HTTP 200, valid page, no results ever |

## The limit of these fixtures, stated plainly

A written fixture tests the parser against **our understanding** of the
markup, not against the markup. If the understanding is wrong, these tests are
green and the product is broken.

That gap is covered by `corpus_test.go`, which runs the parser against real
captured pages held outside this repository. See its comment for how to point
it at your own captures. Run it whenever Google changes something, and before
trusting a release.
